statement: NDC names droughts, floods and heatwaves as major disasters, lists drought seasons in 2012-13, 2015-16, 2018-19 and 2023-24, and says drought exposure varies across Zimbabwe.
compact_statement: NDC names droughts, floods and heatwaves as major disasters, lists drought seasons in 2012-13, 2015-16, 2018-19 and 2023-24, and says drought exposure varies across Zimbabwe.
affected_groups: communities dependent on climate-sensitive natural resources

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 12 (printed p. 7), climate hazards and recent droughts

uncertainty: The passage gives season dates and national variation but no district impact counts.

statement: NDC locates flood exposure in low-lying areas, dam overflows, river confluences, upstream backwater and cyclone paths; floods have spread to previously unaffected areas.
compact_statement: NDC locates flood exposure in low-lying areas, dam overflows, river confluences, upstream backwater and cyclone paths; floods have spread to previously unaffected areas.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 12 (printed p. 7), flood locations and events

uncertainty: NDC provides hazard locations, not mapped population exposure or loss totals in this passage.

statement: NDC reports that the National Adaptation Plan identifies 18 priority outputs across seven sectors, including agriculture, water, health, infrastructure and human settlements.
compact_statement: NDC reports that the National Adaptation Plan identifies 18 priority outputs across seven sectors, including agriculture, water, health, infrastructure and human settlements.
uncertainty: Reported NAP priorities are not evidence that actions were implemented or effective.

statement: World Bank says agriculture employs 70 percent of Zimbabwe's population; reliance on rainfed systems and maize leaves the sector vulnerable to climate events, especially ENSO-linked droughts.
compact_statement: World Bank says agriculture employs 70 percent of Zimbabwe's population; reliance on rainfed systems and maize leaves the sector vulnerable to climate events, especially ENSO-linked droughts.

source_refs.locator: Official World Bank page, agriculture sector profile

uncertainty: National sector profile; no household or regional disaggregation on the page.

statement: World Bank attributes the 2023-24 severe drought to El Nino and reports maize yield 60 percent below the five-year average, alongside widespread food insecurity and economic hardship.
compact_statement: World Bank attributes the 2023-24 severe drought to El Nino and reports maize yield 60 percent below the five-year average, alongside widespread food insecurity and economic hardship.

source_refs.locator: Official World Bank page, 2023-2024 drought impact

uncertainty: Page gives a national yield comparison; district variation and method are not shown.

statement: World Bank reports that the 2023-24 El Nino drought caused about US$363 million in damage and losses.
compact_statement: World Bank reports that the 2023-24 El Nino drought caused about US$363 million in damage and losses.

source_refs.locator: Official World Bank page, 2023-2024 drought damage estimate

uncertainty: Press page reports the estimate without presenting its calculation method.

statement: Source dated 2024-05 reports: The appeal documents a February 2024 dry spell exceeding 30 days; its cover caption identifies wilting, prematurely maturing maize in Zvimba District.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-05 reports: The appeal documents a February 2024 dry spell exceeding 30 days; its cover caption identifies wilting, prematurely maturing maize in Zvimba District.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 3 photograph caption and PDF p. 6, ‘Context Overview.’

uncertainty: The photograph caption is a site example, not a district-wide crop-loss estimate.

statement: Source dated 2024-05 reports: The appeal assessed drought-related food and water insecurity as heightening GBV, sexual-exploitation and child-marriage risks; it links long water-collection journeys for women and girls to greater sexual-violence exposure.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-05 reports: The appeal assessed drought-related food and water insecurity as heightening GBV, sexual-exploitation and child-marriage risks; it links long water-collection journeys for women and girls to greater sexual-violence exposure.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 6, context overview and drought protection-risk assessment.

uncertainty: A May 2024 qualitative protection-risk assessment, not measured GBV/child-marriage incidence, a current risk trend or climate-attributable violence.

statement: Source dated 2024-12 reports: UNICEF reported 6,028 water points broken and 2,310 identified sources dry in 2024, primarily in Masvingo, Matabeleland South and Midlands provinces.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-12 reports: UNICEF reported 6,028 water points broken and 2,310 identified sources dry in 2024, primarily in Masvingo, Matabeleland South and Midlands provinces.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1), water-source paragraph and footnote 11 citing July 2024 water-point updates.

uncertainty: Countrywide July 2024 water-point counts, concentrated mainly but not entirely in the named provinces; no province-specific counts are inferred.

statement: Source dated 2024-12 reports: The appeal reports child-wasting prevalence rose from 4.1% to 4.9% in rural areas and 3.0% to 5.6% in urban areas between 2023 and 2024.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-12 reports: The appeal reports child-wasting prevalence rose from 4.1% to 4.9% in rural areas and 3.0% to 5.6% in urban areas between 2023 and 2024.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1), ‘Humanitarian Situation and Needs.’

uncertainty: Rural/urban aggregates are not district-specific; the source does not causally attribute the trend.

statement: Source dated 2024-12 reports: A UNICEF outreach in Sanyati identified a severely malnourished seven-year-old; her family lived 38 km from the nearest clinic, and the report says drought-related food insecurity and disrupted facility access left children vulnerable.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024-12 reports: A UNICEF outreach in Sanyati identified a severely malnourished seven-year-old; her family lived 38 km from the nearest clinic, and the report says drought-related food insecurity and disrupted facility access left children vulnerable.
institutions: Ministry of Health and Child Care

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1), ‘Story from the Field: Sanyati district.’

uncertainty: One household access example, not district prevalence or generalizable causal attribution; no personal identity is needed for app retrieval.

statement: Source dated 2025-03-19 reports: In drought-prone Mwenezi, Pikinini Jawanda lead farmer Chizivano Shava combines runoff trenches, infiltration pits, rainwater capture and two tanks totaling 130,000 litres; his wife reports less distant water collection and enough for household and garden use.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-03-19 reports: In drought-prone Mwenezi, Pikinini Jawanda lead farmer Chizivano Shava combines runoff trenches, infiltration pits, rainwater capture and two tanks totaling 130,000 litres; his wife reports less distant water collection and enough for household and garden use.

source_refs.locator: UNDP story, ‘A Climate-Proofed Homestead in the Heart of Drylands,’ Mwenezi and Pikinini Jawanda sections.

uncertainty: Named project participant and spouse accounts; no independent measurement of household water access or yield effects.

statement: Source dated 2025-03-19 reports: UNDP reported 230 Farmer Field Schools across 15 project districts and 54,284 rain-fed hectares using water-harvesting measures in 2024; seven irrigation schemes covering 527 hectares had been climate-proofed.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-03-19 reports: UNDP reported 230 Farmer Field Schools across 15 project districts and 54,284 rain-fed hectares using water-harvesting measures in 2024; seven irrigation schemes covering 527 hectares had been climate-proofed.
geographies: 15 Climate Resilient Livelihoods project districts in southern Zimbabwe

source_refs.locator: UNDP story, ‘Scaling Up: Climate-Proofing Agriculture for the Future.’

uncertainty: Implementer-reported reach and works; no independent results evaluation or district-level output breakdown is given.

statement: Source dated 2026-09-17 reports: The September 2026 mission reported that Pikinini-Jawanda's 156-hectare scheme supports 300 farmers from 12 villages; farmers diversified crops and maintained production and financial records to manage the shared investment.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-09-17 reports: The September 2026 mission reported that Pikinini-Jawanda's 156-hectare scheme supports 300 farmers from 12 villages; farmers diversified crops and maintained production and financial records to manage the shared investment.

source_refs.locator: UNDP report, ‘When reliable water unlocks opportunity,’ Pikinini-Jawanda Irrigation Scheme, Mwenezi.

uncertainty: GCF mission and project reporting; no independent beneficiary survey or yield comparison is reported.

statement: Source dated 2026-09-17 reports: UNDP reports expansion of Vimbanayi from 23 to 35 hectares with improved water abstraction, storage and conveyance; a scheme leader said farmers now produce maize, chilli, sugar beans and vegetables with more income streams.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-09-17 reports: UNDP reports expansion of Vimbanayi from 23 to 35 hectares with improved water abstraction, storage and conveyance; a scheme leader said farmers now produce maize, chilli, sugar beans and vegetables with more income streams.

source_refs.locator: UNDP report, ‘From water to production—and production to livelihoods,’ Vimbanayi Irrigation Scheme, Chipinge.

uncertainty: Implementer report with an attributed scheme-leader account; no counterfactual or household income estimate is provided.

statement: Source dated 2026-09-17 reports: At Makoholi, 15 Farmer Field Schools and 56 demonstration plots directly reach 330 farmers and share learning with about 1,500 others; 188 extension officers have trained in fodder harvesting and feed formulation.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-09-17 reports: At Makoholi, 15 Farmer Field Schools and 56 demonstration plots directly reach 330 farmers and share learning with about 1,500 others; 188 extension officers have trained in fodder harvesting and feed formulation.

source_refs.locator: UNDP report, ‘Where innovation meets the farmer,’ Makoholi Innovation Platform.

uncertainty: Mission-reported training and reach, not an independent assessment of uptake or impact.

statement: Source dated 2024 reports: A 2024 stakeholder workshop framed water scarcity and artisanal mining as contributors to resource tensions, and identified climate-related livelihood shocks, displacement and harmful coping as pathways that may destabilize communities and strain host-area services.
compact_statement: Source dated 2024 reports: A 2024 stakeholder workshop framed water scarcity and artisanal mining as contributors to resource tensions, and identified climate-related livelihood shocks, displacement and harmful coping as pathways that may destabilize communities and strain host-area services.

source_refs.locator: Official publication page, shared-vision summary, paragraph introducing four climate-security pathways.

uncertainty: A workshop-derived shared-vision summary, not tested causal mechanisms, a named local conflict case or evidence of climate-caused violence.
